concept.title: Shadows, opacity, transforms and masks
concept.shortdesc: Effects change how an element is drawn without changing what it is. They make it transparent, move it, turn it or scale it, cut parts of it away, fade it with a mask, and mix it with what is behind it. This chapter shows how to apply them to the elements of an SVG drawing. The effects reference at the end lists the properties.

conbody.p: An effect belongs to an element and to everything inside it. When you turn a group, its shapes turn with it. When you make a group transparent, CSSMedia first draws the whole group as one picture and then makes that picture transparent, so shapes that overlap inside the group do not show through each other.

CSSMedia applies the effects of this chapter to the elements of a drawing: shapes, text, images, groups, use elements and nested svg elements. The drawing itself comes from your XML or from a file, as the SVG chapter explains.

conbody.p: You set an effect with a rule of a style sheet, as with any other property. The SVG elements of a drawing have more ways to set style, which Style a drawing explains.

CSSMedia applies the effects of an element in a fixed order. First it places the element with its transform. Then it cuts the element with its clip, fades it with its mask, and finally draws it with its opacity and blend mode. The clip and the mask are in the transformed coordinates, so they move with the element.
